newsitem.title: USA: Continental Airlines orders Boeing aircraft, mulls buyback. [CORRECTED 08:15 GMT 12/10]
newsitem.headline: Continental Airlines orders Boeing aircraft, mulls buyback. [CORRECTED 08:15 GMT 12/10]

text.p: Continental Airlines Thursday announced a $2 billion (Corrects from $450 million) order for 60 jet planes from Boeing Co.
Delivery of the 30 Boeing 737-500 and 30 Boeing 737-600 twinjet aircraft is to begin in 1997 and continue through 1999.
Separately, Continental Chairman Gordon Bethune said Thursday that carrier was considering a plan to buy back stock. Bethune did not specify the size or timing of a possible buy-back.
"We're in talks about a share buy-back," Bethune said during a presentation with industry analysts. "It's something every responsible company should consider."

The aircraft in the latest order are powered by CFM56-3 and CFM56-7 turbofan engines, which are produced by CFM International. CFMI is a 50/50 joint company of Snecma of France and General Electric of the United States.
